verdicts.reason: A uses the banner width with a readable two-line headline, but the CTA sits on the far left ahead of the headline, so the reading order is reversed and the message comes after the action. B shrinks the original's stacked layout into the strip: the headline is tiny, the button is jammed against the bottom edge with no breathing room, and both sides are left empty.

A is a proper left-to-right banner: a large, legible headline on the left, then the CTA pill on the right with sensible margins. The only polish needed is that the headline almost touches the top and bottom edges. B is the same squeezed centred stack as before, with tiny headline text, a button crammed at the bottom edge and large dead space on the left and right.

A has the right banner order (headline, then CTA on the right), but the button is undersized and its label is barely legible. The headline block also floats right of centre, leaving an empty area on the left that makes the layout lopsided. B is again the shrunken centred stack: small text, a CTA touching the bottom edge, and a layout that ignores the wide format.
